description_full: Meridian Energy Limited engages in the renewable electricity generation and retail business to residential, business, and industrial customers in New Zealand. The company generates electricity through 7 hydro power stations; 8 wind farms; and 100MW battery energy storage system, as well as solar array. It sells electricity under the Meridian and Powershop brands. It also offers EV charging solutions; and software development, professional, and insurance services, as well as act as a licence holder and non-trading entity. The company was formerly known as Hydro Energy Limited. Meridian Energy Limited was incorporated in 1998 and is based in Wellington, New Zealand.

financial_summary: Meridian Energy LTD is a mid-cap utilities business with a $8.0B market cap on $2.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 5% against a 6% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 100% confirm genuine pricing power.
The business throws off $303M in free cash flow — roughly 14 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.9× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 8.5×.

Shareholder yield of 2.6% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 52% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
